obligations.condition: With the function registered, the control (no claim) completes a phone MFA finalize before the hook observations; the ID token names the control through claims and a derived lookup.
Password sign-in of the account carrying the disabling claim while the function answers disabled: true. Accepted and refused are both valid observations; the row is always executed.
If tokens were returned, accounts:lookup with the ID token names the account; executed exactly when the first sign-in was accepted.
If tokens were returned, the refresh token is redeemed and the derived ID token names the account; executed exactly when the first sign-in was accepted.
The disabled flag of the account as read through privileged accounts:lookup immediately after the first sign-in, recorded true or false.
A second password sign-in of the same account, still under the function; accepted and refused are both valid.
Phone MFA finalize of the account carrying the disabling claim: the function runs after the second factor. Accepted and refused are both valid; the row is always executed.
If tokens were returned, accounts:lookup with the ID token names the account; executed exactly when the finalize was accepted.
If tokens were returned, the refresh token is redeemed; executed exactly when the finalize was accepted.
The disabled flag of the MFA account as read through privileged accounts:lookup immediately after the finalize, recorded true or false.
A second password sign-in of the MFA account; accepted (a pending credential) and refused are both valid.
After the hook observations the control completes another phone MFA finalize, bounding the run against an environment-wide failure.

limitations: URLs were read during design; no new frozen full-body source snapshot or completed page-review claim is made by this mapping.

The sources document that a blocking function may set disabled on the user and that beforeSignIn runs after the second factor and before the ID token is returned; they do not state whether the request in which the function disables the user is refused or completed. The observation, not the sources, answers that for the recorded conditions.

One function shape (a disabling response for a claim) deployed with the first-generation API; no rejecting function, no beforeCreate, no other response fields, no tenant, one run. The persisted flag was read back once immediately; no wait or second readback.

The oracle project's blocking trigger, MFA, phone sign-in and SMS region configuration were changed for the run and restored; the restore readback and whole-configuration digest comparison are part of the receipt.
No execution approval, independent signature verification, SDK or Rules claim follows from this mapping.
